No, it didn't: three of the six services broke the conventions. I fixed them in `docker-compose.yml`, and all six now have a `mem_limit` and a pinned version tag.

| Service | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `cache` | no `mem_limit` | added `mem_limit: 256m` |
| `worker` | image `stockroom/worker:latest`, no `mem_limit` | pinned to `1.3.2`, added `mem_limit: 512m` |
| `proxy` | image `nginx:latest` | pinned to `nginx:1.28` |

`web`, `api` and `db` were already compliant.

The file parses, but I did not start the stack or pull the images. Nothing in the repo dictated the new values, so please check them:

- **`worker` at `1.3.2`**: this matches `VERSION` and the `web` and `api` images. I assumed a `stockroom/worker:1.3.2` tag is published.
- **`nginx:1.28`**: this is the stable line as far as I know. If `latest` was resolving to a mainline build in your deployment, pin to that version instead to avoid a silent downgrade.
- **Memory limits (`256m` cache, `512m` worker)**: these are my estimates, sized against the neighbouring services. Adjust them to actual usage; a cache limit that is too low will get Valkey OOM-killed unless it also has a matching `maxmemory` setting.
